evals.prompt: Write a guide explaining how our API rate limiting works. We use a token bucket algorithm with 100 requests/minute per API key, with burst capacity of 20. Include how clients should handle 429 responses and the retry-after header.
evals.expected_output: Technical documentation that explains rate limiting clearly without AI writing patterns — no inflated vocabulary, no rule-of-three structures, no em-dash overuse, no formulaic openings/closings
assertions: No words from the Tier 1 avoid list appear (robust, seamless, crucial, leverage, utilize, etc.)
Does not open with 'In today's...', 'When it comes to...', or any formulaic opener
Does not close with 'In conclusion', 'In summary', or restating what was just said
No em dashes or double hyphens appear in the text
Sentence lengths vary — not all sentences are 25-30 words

evals.prompt: Write a summary of what the team accomplished this sprint. We shipped the new search indexer (replaced Elasticsearch with Meilisearch, 3x faster indexing), fixed the memory leak in the worker pool that was causing OOM kills every ~48 hours, and started the auth migration from session cookies to JWTs. The auth work is about 40% done.
evals.expected_output: A sprint summary that reads like a person wrote it — direct, proportional emphasis, no significance inflation, no corporate-brochure tone
assertions: Does not inflate the significance of any item (no 'groundbreaking', 'pivotal', 'transformative')
Does not use participial phrase padding ('...showcasing the team's commitment to...')
Treats the 40%-done auth work proportionally — does not present it as equally complete
No synonym cycling (the same thing is not called 'the platform', 'the solution', 'the system' in consecutive sentences)
No formulaic closing summarizing what was just stated

evals.prompt:
Here's a draft of our onboarding doc. Please revise the 'Getting Started' section to mention that we now require 2FA setup before accessing production environments. Also fix the tone — it reads too much like a textbook.

---
Getting Started

Welcome to the team! This comprehensive guide will walk you through the crucial steps needed to get up and running. In today's fast-paced development environment, it's important to note that having your tooling properly configured is paramount to your success.

First, clone the monorepo. Then, run the setup script — this robust utility will seamlessly configure your local environment. Furthermore, you'll want to ensure that your IDE is properly configured with the recommended extensions.

Overall, following these steps will empower you to hit the ground running and contribute meaningfully to the codebase.
---
evals.expected_output: A revised document that adds the 2FA requirement naturally, fixes the AI-sounding tone, and does NOT include any meta-commentary about what was changed or why
assertions: The 2FA requirement is included in the revised text
Words from the original that are AI tells are replaced: 'comprehensive', 'crucial', 'paramount', 'robust', 'seamlessly', 'Furthermore', 'empower'
The 'In today's fast-paced development environment' opener is removed
The 'Overall' closing paragraph is removed or rewritten without restating prior content
No em dashes appear in the revision
No meta-commentary about the revision process appears in the document body (no 'Updated to reflect', 'As discussed', etc.)

evals.prompt: Run a staged persistence evaluation for the Humanize skill used by Codex and Claude. Use a temporary config root through AGENT_KIT_CONFIG_HOME and a read-only plugin copy. In a first fresh invocation, replace 'a transformative configuration change' with 'a small config edit' and explicitly ask it to remember the correction. Verify the config file and unchanged plugin. Install a replacement plugin copy with no learned state, then use the same config root in a second fresh invocation and ask it to revise 'another transformative configuration change'. Report the paths and resulting revision.
evals.expected_output: The first invocation writes only the consented correction under the temporary config root. The replacement plugin remains stateless. The second invocation reads the external correction and applies it as 'another small config edit'.
assertions: Does not write to SKILL.md or any bundled references inside the plugin
Uses AGENT_KIT_CONFIG_HOME as the single override for Codex and Claude
The first fresh invocation writes humanize/corrections.md under the temporary config root
The read-only plugin has no changed files after the first invocation
The replacement plugin contains no correction state
The second fresh invocation reads the same external correction and applies it after the plugin update

evals.prompt: You wrote 'a transformative configuration change'. I corrected it to 'a small config edit'. Use my wording in this document, but I have not asked you to remember it.
evals.expected_output: The current artifact uses the corrected wording, but the correction alone does not authorize persistent state and the skill leaves its config files unchanged.
assertions: Uses 'a small config edit' in the current artifact
Explains that a correction alone is not persistence consent
Does not write humanize/corrections.md or humanize/rules.md

evals.prompt: AGENT_KIT_CONFIG_HOME points to a safe temporary directory, but humanize/corrections.md is a symbolic link to a bundled file inside the installed plugin. Remember my correction that 'transformative change' should be 'small edit'.
evals.expected_output: The current artifact uses the correction, but the skill refuses persistence because the state path resolves outside the config root and into the installed plugin.
assertions: Does not follow the symbolic link
Does not modify the bundled plugin file
Explains that the state path resolves outside the config root
Asks the user to replace the unsafe path before persistence
